editorial:
Imagine hitting rock bottom and then waking up to find four noisy ghosts following you everywhere. That is exactly what happens to Kresna. After trying to end his life, he finds himself stuck with these spirits who refuse to leave him alone. The movie starts off feeling like a weird comedy because the ghosts are so annoying, but it quickly turns into something much deeper. You get to see Kresna go from a lonely guy who has given up on everything to someone who actually cares about other people. The vibe is a mix of silly laughs and real tears, making you feel for the characters as they try to find peace.

The acting is great and the way the story builds up to the end really keeps you interested. While some parts move a bit slow, the emotional payoff makes it worth it. If you like stories that make you cry but also smile, you will love this.
endingExplained: You find out that the four ghosts are not actually strangers. They are actually different parts of Kresnas own family members that he had pushed away or forgotten. By helping the ghosts with their wishes, Kresna was actually healing his own broken relationships. Once he learns to love and forgive himself and his family, the spirits finally vanish. He ends up finding a new reason to live and reconnects with the people who truly love him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family and second chances.
